headline_marked: [[PM Tareque Rahman visits Kishoreganj]] for first time since oath, to launch projects & distribute aid
headline: PM Tareque Rahman visits Kishoreganj for first time since oath, to launch projects & distribute aid
summary: Prime Minister Tareque Rahman is on his first visit to Kishoreganj since taking oath, participating in various development programs including family card distribution, tree planting, and inaugurating the National Fisheries Week 2026.
details: Prime Minister Tareque Rahman is making his first visit to Kishoreganj since taking oath. During his visit, he will participate in various development programs across the district.

His itinerary includes inspecting Kishoreganj Sadar, Katiadi, and Pakundia upazilas. He will begin by releasing fish fry into the Old Brahmaputra River at Mirzapur Chairmanbari Ghat in Pakundia around 11:30 AM.

The Prime Minister will then visit the Katiadi Carp Hatchery Complex at 12:30 PM. Following this, he will inaugurate the National Fisheries Week 2026 and distribute awards at Achmita George Institution field around 1:00 PM.

In the afternoon, at 4:00 PM, the Prime Minister will distribute family cards and various grants at the Old Stadium in Kishoreganj district town. He is also scheduled to inaugurate the honorarium distribution program for Imams, Muezzins, and other religious workers at the same event.

Additionally, around 2:30 PM, he will inaugurate the development project of the historic Sholakia Eidgah. He will also participate in a tree-planting program organized by the Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal.
Extensive preparations have been undertaken in Kishoreganj for the Prime Minister's arrival. Various roads in Sadar, Katiadi, and Pakundia have been repaired and cleaned in anticipation of his visit.

This being his inaugural visit to Kishoreganj since assuming office, it has generated significant enthusiasm among party activists and the general public. The Prime Minister is expected to depart Kishoreganj for Dhaka around 6:00 PM.

headline: BCS viva changing to competency-based interviews to assess practical skills, PSC Chairman announces
summary: The Bangladesh Public Service Commission is moving away from traditional interviews to a globally recognized competency-based system. This reform aims to evaluate candidates' real-world skills and suitability for government service, not just academic knowledge
details: For years, BCS oral examinations focused on traditional questions about self-introduction, academic subjects, cadre details, and general knowledge. However, the Bangladesh Public Service Commission (PSC) is now introducing a major change to this established system.

PSC Chairman Professor Mobasher Monem announced that the commission is adopting the internationally recognized 'Competency-Based Interview' (CBI) method alongside conventional oral exams. This approach is globally popular and proven for assessing a candidate's practical skills and suitability for government cadre service.

This transformation is part of PSC's broader administrative and examination system reforms, with commission members already undergoing necessary training. Competency refers to a candidate's ability, capability, and practical application skills, which are crucial for government officials.

Unlike traditional interviews, CBI delves into real-life scenarios to evaluate how candidates handle challenges, make decisions, resolve conflicts, and work in teams. For instance, instead of asking "Are you a good leader?", a CBI question might be, "Describe a situation where team members disagreed; how did you manage it?"

This method requires candidates to provide concrete examples from their past experiences, allowing the board to analyze their actual behavior and decision-making processes. The core philosophy is that past actions and decisions are the best indicators of future performance in complex real-world situations.

New graduates should not be apprehensive, as CBI does not solely depend on prior job experience. Diverse life experiences, such as involvement in clubs, event management, volunteer work, or resolving personal crises, are all considered relevant "work experiences" for this assessment.

Globally, competency-based interviews are highly regarded in government recruitment, with countries like Canada and South Africa explicitly incorporating them into their hiring guidelines. This approach ensures that officials are not just good at written exams but also effective in practical complexities.

To prepare, candidates must shift their focus from textbooks to recalling and documenting their past life experiences. They should list instances of challenges faced, successes achieved, leadership roles, teamwork, problem-solving, decision-making, and communication skills.
